Ruling

Partial refund PARTIAL_REFUND

Refund to the rider: SGD 3.45

The judge's explanation, as written

Rider, your dispute of the metered fare is upheld in part; Driver, the excess distance on this trip is not excused. THE DEVIATION. This was trip TRP-02802 (11 Sep 2026, Northpoint City to Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4), a metered fare, with a booked optimal route of 11.4 km. POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure where the trace and the trip record disagree: EV-GPS-02802 records 14.56 km against the trip record's rounded 14.60 km copy. The excess is 3.16 km, or 27.72% of optimal, which clears both establishment gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL (3.16 km is below 8.0 km and 27.72% is below 50%), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 295 trips, far below the pattern thresholds, and POL-GEN-01 confines that check to those two fields only. No driver-conduct referral arises. TRACE QUALITY. The trace carries 115 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds. It fails none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so it is not impaired for policy purposes, the excess is measured on it directly, and no independent corroboration is required. THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE. Driver, your statement that traffic was heavy so you took another road is an external-traffic-cause excuse. Under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. That advisory, EV-ADVIS-02802-01, is MISSING (no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13, the assertion carries no weight. It neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. No rider-requested detour applies (chat log EV-CHAT-02802 carries 0 messages, POL-RD-04), no pickup or drop-off amendment applies (POL-RD-05), and this is not a pooled trip (vehicle type RYDE_X, POL-RD-12). WHY THIS DOES NOT ESCALATE. The driver's side asks that the case be held under POL-RD-10(5) because the advisory identifier is missing. I decline. POL-RD-13 addresses this exact situation: where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory, the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5) - the absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it, and the deviation stands at the measured figure with POL-RD-02 running against the booked 11.4 km optimal. The driver's own statement names no advisory, and the minted identifier is cited on both sides only as an absence, not as the ground of the excuse. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across the three artifacts, the trace is not impaired, the timestamps agree, and no charge line is unmatched. THE REFUND (POL-RD-02). The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02802), so POL-RD-11 does not apply; the surge multiplier of 1.0 was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier. charged_total = 20.87. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 11.4 + 0.28 x 15.4) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 16.6620 + 0.80 = 17.4620. Refund = 20.87 - 17.4620 = 3.4080, rounded up to SGD 3.45. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 16.3% of charged_total, below the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND. POL-RD-09 adds nothing separate: there are no ERP gantry lines, no airport surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo, so nothing is double-counted. On the rider's plea of SGD 2.50, the contested sum is the rider's own estimate, not the policy measure; POL-RD-02 defines the refund as charged_total less the recomputed fare, and on this fare that is SGD 3.45. OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.45 to the rider; no driver compensation and no referrals. The monetary effect is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue. All artifacts carrying the deciding facts sit at full weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped. Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

The driver advocate

kept The distance actually driven is governed by the GPS polyline, not by the rounded convenience copy on the trip record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 14.56 km against a booked optimal of 11.4 km, an excess of 3.16 km and 27.72% — not the 3.20 km a reading of trip_record.actual_distance_km would give. That excess clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km), but it falls below both of the clause's MATERIAL gates, 8.0 km absolute and 50%, so no material deviation is recorded against this driver and the POL-RD-06 profile check is not even triggered by this trip.

evidence EV-GPS-02802, EV-TRIP-02802 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept Even if the POL-RD-06 check were run, it is answered on the two fields that clause permits and it clears the driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 295, so the ratio is 0.00 against the 0.05 threshold and the flag count is below the 3 the clause requires. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift of the POL-RD-02 figure and no driver-conduct referral arising from this trip. No other profile field is used for that conclusion, because POL-GEN-01 makes the remaining fields context only.

evidence EV-DPROF-02802 · clauses POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01

kept The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 115 fixes at a 10 s sampling interval, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds. It therefore fails none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c), no impairment discount or corroboration requirement attaches to it, and the excess is directly measurable on the trace itself.

evidence EV-GPS-02802 · clauses POL-RD-07

kept There is nothing on this fare for POL-RD-09 to correct as a pass-through: erp_gantries is empty, the off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.0, waiting_time_fee is 0.0 and promo_discount is 0.0. The rider therefore obtains no standalone pass-through refund and no billing-integrity finding on this record, and any recovery is confined to the distance-and-time arithmetic of POL-RD-02.

evidence EV-FARE-02802 · clauses POL-RD-09

kept This is a metered trip, not a quoted one: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so no upfront-quote entitlement arises. The rider's assertion that the app 'quoted 11.4 km' is not a contractual quotation of distance or price — 11.4 km is the routing-engine optimal stored on the trip record at booking, and it is an input to the POL-RD-02 arithmetic rather than a promise of the route or the fare.

evidence EV-FARE-02802, EV-TRIP-02802 · clauses POL-RD-11

kept Whatever is decided, the money in issue is small and bounded, and the driver asks the tribunal to say so on the face of the ruling. charged_total is 20.87; the POL-RD-02 recomputed fare on this record — 3.80 base plus 0.75 x 11.4 km plus 0.28 x 15.4 min, at the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo — is 17.4620; the difference is 3.4080, rounded up to SGD 3.45, and the de minimis floor of 0.50 is not engaged. That is 16.3% of the amount charged, far below the 90% share that would make FULL_REFUND the outcome, so the outcome can only be PARTIAL_REFUND; and under POL-GEN-03 a PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the contested amount, which the rider pleaded at SGD 2.50.

evidence EV-FARE-02802 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-GEN-03

kept The driver's explanation is an external-cause one — heavy traffic, so another road — and the only artifact that could test it is the traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-02802-01, which is MISSING from the pool: no payload, admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03's test cannot be run on this record at all, so the excuse is neither made out nor refuted by any evidence. That is the situation POL-RD-10(5) is written for — an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool — and POL-RD-13(1) expressly declines to narrow POL-RD-10(5) where the party does cite the missing identifier, as the driver cites it here. The disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer under POL-GEN-03 rather than refunded on an excuse the bundle cannot test; and if the tribunal declines to escalate, the honest consequence is that the excuse is discarded under POL-RD-13(2) and the excess stands at no more than the SGD 3.45 arithmetic set out above.

evidence EV-ADVIS-02802-01, EV-GPS-02802 · clauses POL-RD-10, POL-RD-13, POL-RD-03

Rider, your dispute of the metered fare is upheld in part; Driver, the excess distance on this trip is not excused. THE DEVIATION. This was trip TRP-02802 (11 Sep 2026, Northpoint City to Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4), a metered fare, with a booked optimal route of 11.4 km. POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure where the trace and the trip record disagree: EV-GPS-02802 records 14.56 km against the trip record's rounded 14.60 km copy. The excess is 3.16 km, or 27.72% of optimal, which clears both establishment gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL (3.16 km is below 8.0 km and 27.72% is below 50%), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 295 trips, far below the pattern thresholds, and POL-GEN-01 confines that check to those two fields only. No driver-conduct referral arises. TRACE QUALITY. The trace carries 115 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds. It fails none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so it is not impaired for policy purposes, the excess is measured on it directly, and no independent corroboration is required. THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE. Driver, your statement that traffic was heavy so you took another road is an external-traffic-cause excuse. Under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. That advisory, EV-ADVIS-02802-01, is MISSING (no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13, the assertion carries no weight. It neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. No rider-requested detour applies (chat log EV-CHAT-02802 carries 0 messages, POL-RD-04), no pickup or drop-off amendment applies (POL-RD-05), and this is not a pooled trip (vehicle type RYDE_X, POL-RD-12). WHY THIS DOES NOT ESCALATE. The driver's side asks that the case be held under POL-RD-10(5) because the advisory identifier is missing. I decline. POL-RD-13 addresses this exact situation: where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory, the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5) - the absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it, and the deviation stands at the measured figure with POL-RD-02 running against the booked 11.4 km optimal. The driver's own statement names no advisory, and the minted identifier is cited on both sides only as an absence, not as the ground of the excuse. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across the three artifacts, the trace is not impaired, the timestamps agree, and no charge line is unmatched. THE REFUND (POL-RD-02). The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02802), so POL-RD-11 does not apply; the surge multiplier of 1.0 was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier. charged_total = 20.87. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 11.4 + 0.28 x 15.4) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 16.6620 + 0.80 = 17.4620. Refund = 20.87 - 17.4620 = 3.4080, rounded up to SGD 3.45. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 16.3% of charged_total, below the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND. POL-RD-09 adds nothing separate: there are no ERP gantry lines, no airport surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo, so nothing is double-counted. On the rider's plea of SGD 2.50, the contested sum is the rider's own estimate, not the policy measure; POL-RD-02 defines the refund as charged_total less the recomputed fare, and on this fare that is SGD 3.45. OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.45 to the rider; no driver compensation and no referrals. The monetary effect is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue. All artifacts carrying the deciding facts sit at full weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped. Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The facts that decide this case — the deviation and the fare — rest on EV-GPS-02802, EV-TRIP-02802 and EV-FARE-02802, all at weight_multiplier 1.0; the only sub-1.0 artifact (the missing advisory at 0.0) carries no deciding fact. To the rider and the driver. The trip ran 14.56 km (EV-GPS-02802) against a booked optimal of 11.4 km (EV-TRIP-02802). POL-RD-01 makes the GPS polyline the governing distance where it disagrees with the rounded copy on the trip record (14.6 km), so the excess is 3.16 km, or 27.72%. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 115 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds; it fails none of POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so the deviation rests on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration. The only traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-02802-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, under POL-RD-08, an assertion of bad traffic that cites no artifact carries no weight. I decline the driver's request to escalate under POL-RD-10(5): POL-RD-13(1) governs, because the driver's own statement names no advisory identifier, and an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one — the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. The fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not close off the distance refund. The refund is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic, read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02802): charged_total 20.87; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.4 + 0.28 x 15.4) x 1.0, the surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 17.4620. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and 16.33% of the amount charged, far below the 90% that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND and not NO_ACTION or FULL_REFUND. Nothing is added on top: no ERP gantry line and no airport surcharge is itemised, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct and nothing is double-counted. The driver's counterparty statement carries no weight multiplier and does not carry the deviation, so it does not move these facts. Confidence 0.90.
